thinking: First I'll dig into the files to see what data is available.

This seems drawn from a real study on IL-33, SARS-CoV-2 and endothelial cells, possibly AstraZeneca's work. Tozorakimab (MEDI3506) is their anti-IL-33 antibody that binds both reduced and oxidized IL-33, and NIP228 is their isotype control. I'm trying to pin down the exact paper, something about IL-33 driving endothelial activation in COVID-19.

It's likely a Cell Press paper on reduced IL-33 activating endothelial cells via ST2 in severe COVID-19, combining HUVEC work, patient serum proteomics and post-mortem lung IHC. Regardless, I'll treat the files as ground truth and decide whether to keep or drop AX-1177 in viral LRTD, which indication the data supports, and which biomarkers, timepoints and next steps to propose. I'm starting to hunt for embedded pitfalls, beginning with the passage mismatch in the methods annex (HUVEC at P2 versus HGMEC at P5).

Each line also comes from a single donor, and only HUVEC has a vehicle arm, so IL-33red versus vehicle exists only there. A549 and MCF7 never get IL-33red, so they only test antibody alone, and the antibody goes in alongside IL-33red without pre-incubation, which may leave blocking incomplete. AveExpr and the empirical Bayes variance are both pooled across all 114 libraries and cell types, which could mislead filtering and distort the endothelial contrasts, so I'm now checking whether the 38 groups and 114 libraries actually add up.

The arm counts check out: 11 endothelial arms and 8 epithelial arms across two timepoints give 38 groups, times three replicates is 114. On the clinical side, the 13 Olink panels aren't reconciled, so proteins like IL-6 could appear on several panels and be double-counted in the BH adjustment. Adjusting for NEWS2 means the ORs only reflect information beyond severity, and log-transforming NPX, which is already log2 and can be negative, looks like a real pitfall.

Serum is another concern, since clotting releases platelet proteins like PF4, CXCL7, VEGF, PDGF, TGF-β, CD40L and P-selectin that could masquerade as endothelial activation, and hemolysis could add noise. The composite endpoint comes from a single-centre, pre-vaccination cohort of 100 with one enrolment sample. For the post-mortem lung blocks, I'll need to fill donor-level fields down from the first block and avoid pseudo-replication across blocks. I also need to watch for single-reader scoring, COVID-negative controls, and comorbidities like COPD or IPF that the pathology text might reveal.

If IL-33 turns out higher in non-COVID chronic lung disease, that would point toward COPD, where tozorakimab is actually in phase 3 alongside its viral LRTD trial. The HGMEC glomerular endothelial cells in the panel also make me wonder whether the data points at diabetic kidney disease, which I think is another tozorakimab indication.

I vaguely recall a Phase IIb trial of MEDI3506 in DKD, possibly one of the FRONTIER studies alongside COPD and asthma, so the glomerular endothelial signal could matter. Still, I should ground the answer in the data itself rather than outside knowledge, and I'm trying to pin down which Cell Press paper these supplementary files come from — possibly the Scott et al. tozorakimab mechanism paper.

There may also be a 2023 iScience paper linking IL-33 to endothelial activation in COVID-19, and the post-mortem lung tissue likely comes from the Arizona Brain and Body Donation Program. That would mean the donor demographics in mmc3 could include neurodegenerative diagnoses, which fits the Neurology panels in the Olink data. Rather than keep speculating, I'll load the files — mmc5 is a 139MB spreadsheet, so I'll check which Python environments are available first.

The singlecell environment has pandas, openpyxl, decoupler and statsmodels, so I'll work there. Calamine or polars might read the 139MB xlsx faster, but openpyxl in read-only mode should be fine. First I'll check each file's sheet names and dimensions.

The 6h sheet in mmc5 has exactly 1,048,576 rows, which is Excel's maximum, so it was almost certainly truncated. That's a real data integrity problem. With 26,210 genes per contrast, the 24h sheet's 629,040 data rows work out to exactly 24 contrasts, but the 6h sheet holds 40 complete contrasts plus a stray 175 rows, so it was cut off partway through a contrast.

Forty-plus contrasts at 6h versus 24 at 24h is odd, so I need to check which contrasts each sheet contains and confirm the last 6h contrast is incomplete. I'll load all of mmc5 in openpyxl read-only mode, which could take a few minutes for about 1.6M rows. Then I'll cache it as parquet or feather if pyarrow is available in the singlecell env.

Interesting: mmc2 hides rows 4 and 16 plus column D, while mmc3 hides several column ranges and has merged cells. The creators are AstraZeneca authors, so this looks like an IL-33/tozorakimab COVID-19 paper. Now I'll pull up mmc2 in full, hidden rows and column D included.

The composite_endpoint_0 and composite_endpoint_1 columns look like per-group fractions: the values work out to multiples of 1/56 and 1/44, so 44 of the 100 patients had the composite endpoint. They're probably the share of samples below LOD (or missing) in each outcome group, and some rows store them as strings. Now I'm checking hidden rows 4 and 16, starting with row 4, which is HGF-ONCII.

Row 4 is HGF on the Oncology II panel and row 16 is IL6-ONCII, both duplicates of proteins measured on other panels. The hidden column D is the lower 95% CI, so I want to see whether any row has a lower bound below 1 despite an adjusted p under 0.05. Next I'll check per-panel assay counts, since 1094 rows falls 102 short of 13×92, and look at proteins like IL6 that repeat across several panels.

The BH adjustment runs across all assays including these duplicates, whose names carry panel-specific suffixes like -ONCII, -CVDII, -IMO, so I'll need to collapse them to unique proteins. I'm also recalling the Olink Inflammation panel's protein list to check whether IL-33 itself is measured, and it does seem to include IL33.

So IL33 sits on the Inflammation panel and ST2 (IL1RL1) on Cardiovascular III, and ST2 comes out second most significant here (OR 3.02 per log unit, adj p 0.0075). That fits IL-33 pathway involvement, but soluble ST2 is a decoy receptor that endothelial cells release under general inflammatory or cardiac stress, so it's fairly non-specific. Now I'm trying to recall which paper this comes from — possibly an AstraZeneca-linked study on IL-33 and endothelial dysfunction in COVID-19.

Other names that come to mind are Natalie van Zuydam, Elizabeth England and Kirsty Houslay, plus the 2023 Sci Rep paper describing tozorakimab as an anti-IL-33 antibody blocking both ST2 and RAGE/EGFR signalling. The "viral LRTD" framing lines up with the ACCORD-2 COVID trial and the Phase 3 TILIA trial in hospitalized viral lung infection. I think the original work showed reduced IL-33 activating endothelial cells, upregulating adhesion molecules and chemokines, with tozorakimab blocking that effect.

They also found severity-linked serum proteins overlapping the IL-33 endothelial signature, plus IL-33 staining in post-mortem COVID lung. These files may contain deliberate traps, though, and I'm meant to treat them as ground truth. So I need a defensible keep-or-drop call, the indication the data points to, next studies, and biomarkers with sampling timepoints and roles (PD, prognostic, predictive). I'll go through all four datasets rigorously, starting with the 6h and 24h HUVEC DEGs and checking for canonical NF-κB targets like VCAM1, ICAM1, SELE, CXCL8, CCL2 and IL6.

I'll also check ST2 (IL1RL1) expression in HUVEC and how big the effects are. In mmc5 I need to list every contrast and check whether the 6h sheet was truncated at Excel's row limit, which could drop key comparisons. The critical one is IL-33red+Compound_47 vs IL-33red+NIP228, alongside antibody-alone effects, the HGMEC response and the A549/MCF7 controls. For the mmc3 IHC, I'll rebuild donor-level data from the merged and hidden cells and aggregate per donor to avoid pseudo-replication before comparing SARS-CoV-2 positive cases.

Then I'll compare against negative donors, noting other pathology diagnoses like COPD or pneumonia. For the mmc2 serum proteomics, I'll reconcile duplicates across panels, check IL33, ST2, overlap with the endothelial signature, LOD fractions and hidden rows. After that I'll weigh whether the data really support COVID-19 LRTD, or instead point to endothelial or kidney disease, or to COPD/asthma via mast cells and eosinophils, starting with a full look at mmc3.

Some of these scores are formulas, like the basal epithelium IL-33 cell averaging 2 and 4.5 to get 3.25, so they're derived values. The conversion columns seem to turn "n+" grades into n+0.5, which pushes values like 5.5 past the stated 0–5 scale, and 5.5 shows up often for IL-33, hinting at a ceiling effect.

Endothelial IL-33 sits at 5.5 in nearly every group, so it can't separate COVID from non-COVID. Donor 1905 is labeled "COVID neg pneumonia" but has no SARS-CoV-2 result recorded, which needs flagging. Donors 1910, 1905, 1970, 1968 and 1961 look like a second batch, with unmerged single blocks, integer IDs and later GHP0027xx block numbers. Next I'll print the truncated rows 19–63 in a more compact format.

Looking at mmc3's structure, I see three groups: COVID-negative pneumonia with 10 donors, COVID-positive pneumonia with 16 donors, and COVID-negative non-pneumonia with 5 donors. Now I'm tallying the rows per COVID-positive donor: most have two, three have eight, and one has a single row.

That gives 49 COVID-positive blocks, 15 COVID-negative pneumonia, and 10 non-pneumonia, for 74 total. Donors 2067, 2072 and 2073 alone supply 24 of the 49 COVID-positive blocks, so any block-level analysis would over-weight them — a pseudo-replication problem. I'm also noticing inconsistent merging: Disease Category is filled on both rows for the first few COVID-positive donors but only the first block elsewhere, and the Notes column's merged ranges (Bronchitis, COPD, Asthma/Rhinitis, Bronchiectasis, etc.) seem to sit on second blocks for some donors like 2045 and 2040, so I'm checking those ranges against donor rows.

...history), so they probably do belong to the donor despite sitting on the wrong row. Other issues: donor 1905 is labeled "COVID neg pneumonia" but has no SARS-CoV-2 status, the 'SARS-Cov-2 ' header has a trailing space, and hidden column D duplicates Sample ID with mixed string/integer types. The derived numeric columns U–W add 0.5 to every non-zero "n+" score, pushing values up to 5.5 beyond the 0–5 scale. The IL-33 values look like averages of two numbers (X2 is literally (2+4.5)/2), which clashes with the annex's claim of a single reader.

More likely the two numbers are the bronchial and bronchiolar sub-scores, given the header, so 4.25 would be "4" averaged with "4+" and 5.5 would be "5+" twice. Either way, 5.5 is off-scale and many values pile up there as a ceiling. Interestingly, nearly all COVID-negative donors hit 5.5 for endothelial IL-33, while COVID-positive donors are lower and more variable, and some even score 0 for vascular smooth muscle (2110, 2060 block A, 2043 block A). That suggests COVID-positive lungs may show less IL-33 staining.

Lower IL-33 staining in COVID+ could mean the alarmin was released from damaged cells, or it could just be tissue damage or autolysis, so it's ambiguous. Either way, it doesn't show IL-33 upregulation. I'll compute donor-level group means per marker and look at the eosinophil and mast cell markers. Non-pneumonia COVID-negative donors lack H&E eosinophils and have low IL-5Rα, while both pneumonia groups show more eosinophils and higher IL-5Rα and NE. That matters because IL-33 drives type 2 inflammation through eosinophils, mast cells and ILC2s.

If those markers rise in pneumonia regardless of COVID status, that's a pneumonia feature, not a COVID one. My recommendation is no: AX-1177 should not stay in the portfolio as a viral LRTD asset, and LRTD development spend should stop. Termination should be the default outcome, after a close-out review of up to 12 weeks that runs no new experiments. The full case is in the committee memo.

## Why
An LRTD programme needs three things to be true. Our data support only the first.

1. **The drug neutralises IL-33 in vitro — strongly supported.**
   - In HUVEC, reduced IL-33 changes 4,031 genes at 6 h. AX-1177 reverses 2,884 of them against the isotype arm (r = −0.80), leaving about 4% of the response.
   - The same programme is blocked in glomerular endothelial cells, although their IL-33 response is inferred because no control arm was run.
   - The antibody alone has no reproducible effect in any of the four cell lines. This is not a safety or developability decision.
2. **IL-33 is active in patients — not shown.**
   - IL-33 itself is missing from the serum data; 100 analysed assays were left out of the file.
   - Lung IL-33 staining does not differ between COVID+ and COVID− pneumonia (per-donor p = 0.92, 0.16 and 0.15 across the three cell types). The scores sit at their ceiling.
3. **IL-33 biology predicts outcome — not shown.**
   - Serum proteins from the IL-33 programme predict ICU, ventilation or death no more often than other proteins (21% vs 17%, p = 0.43).
   - The most endothelium-specific ones (VCAM-1, ICAM-1, E-selectin) don't predict at all.
   - What does predict outcome is intracellular proteins leaking into clotted serum (29% vs 14%, p = 1.5×10⁻⁵).
4. **Scope — COVID-19 only.** All patient data are SARS-CoV-2 (100 patients, before vaccination, one centre). There are no influenza or RSV data.

**Best argument for keeping it:** soluble ST2, the IL-33 decoy receptor, is the #2 outcome predictor of 1,063 proteins (OR 3.02, 95% CI 1.83–5.01; one of two passing Bonferroni). It justifies the close-out, but it is not IL-33-specific. High levels could even mean IL-33 is already neutralised.

## Problems in the data package the committee should know about
- **Serum statistics can't be reproduced.** The false-discovery correction used 1,194 tests but only 1,094 were delivered. At least one left-out assay was a top-20 outcome association.
- **Tissue groups are mislabelled.** Labels contradict the autopsy diagnoses for 7 of 15 COVID-negative donors, and one has no SARS-CoV-2 result.
- **IL-33 tissue scores are unreliable.** The columns were hidden, one cell is a formula, and 53% of endothelial scores exceed the stated 0–5 scale.
- **Gene-level statistics are distorted.** One statistical model was fitted across four cell types, so key endothelial genes with large, mirrored effects (e.g., E-selectin +11 log2FC) are reported non-significant.
- **Gene names are wrong for 1,129 genes.** Lookups by gene name silently miss them; I worked from stable gene IDs instead.

## What we're dropping, and what the data point at
We're dropping a clean IL-33 blocker because the disease premise has no support in our own data. The data point at a mechanism (IL-33 activating blood-vessel lining) and a patient state (hospitalised severe pneumonia with high soluble ST2), not a pathogen: nothing in the tissue is COVID-specific. That is narrower than viral LRTD and untested. They do not support COPD/asthma, kidney or heart failure.

## Biomarkers, sampling and plan
- **Soluble ST2:** ready now for patients, as a baseline marker for enriching or stratifying on risk.
- **Free and drug-bound IL-33:** needed to show the drug reaches its target; not ready (data missing, assay needed).
- **Soluble E-selectin, CCL20, OPG, IL-6:** exploratory markers of drug effect.
- **HGF:** risk covariate only.
- **Timing:** sample at enrolment before dosing (the only timepoint our patient data cover), then 24 h after dosing. In cells the IL-33 response peaks by 6 h and fades by 24 h.
- **Plan:**
  - Close-out, using only data we hold: recover the omitted assays including IL-33, refit the RNA-seq per cell line, and score the 22 lung RNA samples we already have. Continue only if soluble ST2 stays predictive after adjusting for IL-6 and HGF, plus IL-33 or tissue evidence.
  - Then in vitro work: antibody added after IL-33, dose-response, and at least three donors.
  - Then a multi-pathogen patient cohort.

## Considered and ruled out
- Keeping LRTD as is; pivoting straight to a trial; a COVID-specific indication.
- COPD/asthma: no epithelial IL-33 experiments, no tissue difference by COPD/asthma history, type-2 markers null.
- Kidney and heart failure: no supporting patient data.
- Biomarkers: HGF as a drug-effect marker, intracellular proteins, tissue IL-33 staining.
- Analysis shortcuts: per-block tissue statistics, the contrast that shares the IL-33 arm, filtering genes on average expression.

I couldn't access patient-level proteomics, the raw RNA-seq counts, or any in vivo, PK or potency data. Immediate termination without the close-out is also defensible if the committee wants zero further spend.
